references.text: The original instruction to set four rows of gemstones on the breastpiece, with odem (ruby), pitda (topaz), and bareket (emerald) in the first row.
The complete description of the breastpiece's design that God gave to Moses, including all four rows of gemstones representing the twelve tribes of Israel.
The list of materials to be gathered for the sanctuary, including onyx stones and setting stones for the ephod and the breastpiece.
The call to bring onyx stones and setting stones for the ephod and the breastpiece as part of the gifts for the tabernacle.
The description of the foundation stones of the wall of the new Jerusalem, adorned with various gemstones, providing an eschatological parallel to the priest's breastpiece.
This verse completes the description of the first row and introduces the second row in the same context as the source verse.
This verse links the twelve tribes (symbolized by the stones in the breastpiece) directly to the foundation wall of the new Jerusalem.
This verse describes the third row of the breastpiece, which is a direct continuation of the list in the source verse.
This verse completes the list of the twelve stones and describes the setting, concluding the theme of the source verse.
This verse uses the same list of gemstones to describe a fallen being, creating a theological contrast to their use in God's holy service.
